title: Grade 12 Physics — Current Electricity & Moving Charges and Magnetism
description: Current Electricity and Moving Charges and Magnetism practice questions
subject: physics

questions.question: Electric current is defined as:
options: Rate of flow of charge (charge per unit time)
questions.explanation: Current I = Q/t (charge per unit time). The SI unit is the Ampere (A), where 1 A = 1 C/s.

questions.question: Resistivity of a material:
options: Depends only on its cross-sectional area
Is a property of the material independent of its dimensions
questions.explanation: Resistivity (ρ) is an intrinsic property of a material — it depends on the material's nature and temperature, not on its shape or size. R = ρL/A.

questions.question: Kirchhoff's current law (KCL) states that:
options: The sum of currents in a loop is zero
The algebraic sum of currents at any junction is zero
Current is always the same in series circuits
Voltage across each branch is equal
questions.explanation: KCL (junction rule): the algebraic sum of currents meeting at a junction is zero: ΣI = 0. This is based on conservation of charge.

questions.question: The Wheatstone bridge is balanced when:
questions.explanation: Wheatstone bridge is balanced (no current through galvanometer) when P/Q = R/S. This allows precise measurement of an unknown resistance.

questions.question: The EMF of a cell is the potential difference when:
options: Two cells are connected in series
questions.explanation: EMF is the potential difference between the terminals of a cell when no current flows (open circuit). When current flows, terminal voltage = EMF − Ir, where r is internal resistance.

questions.question: Temperature coefficient of resistivity for most metals is:
questions.explanation: For most metals (conductors), resistivity increases with temperature (positive temperature coefficient). For semiconductors, resistivity decreases with temperature.

questions.question: A cell of EMF 2 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a 1.5 Ω resistor. The terminal voltage is:
questions.explanation: I = E/(R+r) = 2/(1.5+0.5) = 1 A. Terminal voltage = E − Ir = 2 − 1×0.5 = 1.5 V.

questions.question: Drift velocity of electrons in a conductor is:
options: Equal to the speed of light
questions.explanation: Drift velocity is the average velocity of electrons due to the applied electric field — very small (typically 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁴ m/s). The signal travels fast because the field propagates at near light speed.

questions.question: The magnetic force on a charge q moving with velocity v in field B is:
questions.explanation: Lorentz magnetic force: F = q(v × B) = qvB sin θ, where θ is the angle between v and B. If v is parallel to B, force is zero.

questions.question: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular current loop of radius R carrying current I is:
questions.explanation: By Biot-Savart law, the magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop: B = μ₀I/(2R).

questions.question: Ampere's circuital law relates the line integral of B to:
options: The total current enclosed by the loop
questions.explanation: Ampere's law: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enc. The line integral of B around a closed loop equals μ₀ times the total current enclosed by the loop.

questions.question: A proton and an electron moving with the same velocity enter a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to it. The radius of the proton's circular path compared to the electron's is:
questions.explanation: r = mv/(qB). Both have same charge magnitude and velocity. Since mass of proton >> mass of electron, radius of proton's path >> radius of electron's path.

questions.question: A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences force by:
options: The Ampere force law (F = BIL sin θ)
questions.explanation: F = BIL sin θ, where B is the magnetic field, I is the current, L is the length of conductor, and θ is the angle between L and B. This is the Ampere force.

questions.question: In a galvanometer, the current sensitivity can be increased by:
options: Increasing the number of turns in the coil
Increasing the area of the coil decreases sensitivity
questions.explanation: Current sensitivity of galvanometer = NBA/k, where N = turns, B = field, A = area, k = spring constant. Increasing N, B, or A increases sensitivity; increasing k decreases it.

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic field B is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic field (magnetic flux density) B is the Tesla (T). 1 T = 1 N/(A·m). The Gauss is the CGS unit (1 T = 10⁴ Gauss).
